text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's Liquefied Natural Gas project suffers a major dislocation following a decision by Italy's Enel to cancel a gas purchase contract.
- Port Harcourt airport was closed on Tuesday after the landing gear on a DC 8 cargo plane malfunctioned, causing it to skip the runway with its undercarriage. Nobody was hurt.
- A substance found in northern Niger state may turn out to be an indication of a hydrocarbon deposit, local officials say.

- Defence headquarters says security is being beefed up in the wake of bomb blasts as counter-insurgency experts join the police to investigate Monday's bomb which targeted the Lagos military administrator.
- Uniform port service charges for clearing agents, based on the value of the goods imported, may be revealed in the 1997 budget to curb indiscriminate charging.
- Federal government has approved 3.2 billion naira to be shared among state and local governments immediately.
- 500 workers have been laid off at the African Timber and Plywood Company in southern Delta state.
- The central bank has been urged to define the exclusive role of discount houses in the face of a threat to their survival by some highly liquid commercial banks entering the business.
- Nigeria Ports Authority has beaten its 1996 revenue forecast by 149 percent.
